title: SpliceImpactR maps alternative RNA processing events driving protein functional diversity.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 21419532 (CC-BY-4.0) holds one 4.9 MB zip of the SpliceImpactR R package source. I listed all 273 files: R code plus small test data (8 example rMATS/exon files from synthetic case/control samples, a test GENCODE v45 annotation and sequence CSV, test InterPro and domain-interaction tables, a protein-interaction RDS). There is no atlas or results table across GTEx tissues in it. The Europe PMC supplementary-files endpoint timed out, so I could not see the NAR supplement.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The analysis of 17,350 GTEx v8 (Genotype-Tissue Expression) samples across 54 tissues, downloaded from AnVIL with gen3-client, and the 23 matched tumour/normal TCGA (The Cancer Genome Atlas) colon cancer pairs (dbGaP phs000178). Both raw sources are controlled access. Whether the supplement contains per-event tables is unknown.

a1_downloadable.note: The only deposit is the software package with toy test data (checked). The real inputs, GTEx and TCGA RNA-seq reads, need dbGaP (NIH controlled-access database) approval. The supplement could not be retrieved.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no measured outcome column. Every output (coding change, frameshift, domain gain or loss, predicted protein-interaction change) is computed by the tool from transcript annotation. A label would have to be constructed by running the pipeline.

a3_inputs_present.note: The test files include sequences and coordinates (checked), but only for a toy subset.

a4_units_stated.note: PSI (percent spliced in, the fraction of transcripts including an exon) is unitless and well defined in the test rMATS files.

a5_enough_rows.note: The test data covers 8 toy samples. No full-scale event table is deposited, so there is no verified count.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 5 MB package; full GTEx re-quantification would be terabytes
a6_fits_laptop.note: The deposited files are trivial, but recreating the atlas means aligning GTEx reads, which does not fit a laptop.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: None of the paper's counts (17,350 samples, more than 600 tumour events) can be checked against any deposited file.

a8_label_provenance.note: The candidate labels (protein impact, domain change, predicted interaction rewiring) are rule-based outputs of SpliceImpactR computed from annotation features. Learning them would distil the tool, which is circular.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model, could embed isoform pairs, but there is no measured label to train on

integration.partner_dataset: GTEx isoform expression (controlled raw data; open gene-level TPM only)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not reachable without a deposited per-event table.

honest_claim_h3: A model trained on this would only reproduce SpliceImpactR's annotation-based rules for how an isoform switch changes the encoded protein; it would not learn measured protein function.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use pairs of alternative transcript sequences to predict whether the switch changes protein domains or interactions.
plain_idea.train_on: Pairs of transcript isoforms that differ by one splicing event, with their protein sequences. The number of examples is unknown because no full event table is deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the switch alters the protein's domains or interaction partners. The only 'truth' here is the tool's own annotation-based computation, not a measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Splicing researchers would like fast predictions of isoform function, but without measured labels such a model would only copy the existing tool.

ml_idea: Considered: predict domain or protein-interaction consequences of isoform switches from protein-language-model embeddings. Rejected because the labels are the tool's own deterministic output and the tissue-scale data is controlled access and not deposited.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Listing the Zenodo zip showed only package code and toy test data, which killed the project.

verdict_reason: This is a software-tool paper. The Zenodo deposit is the R package with toy test data, the GTEx and TCGA inputs are dbGaP controlled access, and every possible label is a rule-based output of the tool itself (fails A1, A2, A5 and A8).
